_meta.title: Beverly new growth, 11-year series
_meta.source: Massachusetts DLS Municipal Databank, new growth added to the levy limit (LA-13 basis), FY2016-FY2026.
_meta.notes: New growth = new taxable value added to the levy each year. It stacks on top of the 2.5% levy increase and then itself grows at 2.5% forever after, so it compounds. FY27 actual ($1.95M) is from the budget book, a different source than this DLS series, and is listed separately.

stats.shareOfPriorLevyPct: ~1.2-1.3% recently, just above the 1.2% statewide median.

fy27Actual.note: A good year, near the top of Beverly's normal range, not a new baseline.

cityPlanningAssumption.note: The forecast budgets new growth BELOW the 11-year historical mean of $1.59M. Deliberate conservatism, but it means the city plans for less than it usually delivers. This is the headroom the development strategy works in.

composition.note: Residential vs. commercial/industrial/personal (CIP) share swings year to year (roughly 48-72% CIP in recent years). CIP new growth is higher-margin: it pays taxes without adding students or heavy service demand. Re-derive the exact per-year split from new_growth.xls before publishing specific percentages.
composition.strategicPoint: Tilt development toward commercial/mixed-use for higher yield per dollar of new growth.

target.note: Strategy target for the X1 lever, not a forecast.
target.gapToClose: Roughly one extra mid-sized commercial project per year above normal churn.
target.value: Each $1M of sustained new growth is ~$1M/yr of permanent, compounding revenue. The only lever that compounds and costs residents nothing.
